title: The Grand Duchy of Lithuania
episode: Timothy Snyder: The Making of Modern Ukraine. Class 6: The Grand Duchy of Lithuania
description: Historian Timothy Snyder’s Yale lecture on the Grand Duchy, a pagan Baltic state that in the 1300s grew into the largest country in Europe. Grand Duke Gediminas made Vilnius its capital, and his name is on the castle tower.

title: The old town
description: A short film on Vilnius’s old town, a World Heritage site since 1994 for its mix of Gothic, Renaissance, Baroque, and Classical buildings. Napoleon is said to have wanted to carry St. Anne’s Church back to Paris.

title: An ancient language
episode: Lithuanian | Oldest Survivor of Indo-European [Language Digest]
description: A short introduction to Lithuanian and why linguists prize it: its sounds and word endings are closer to ancient Sanskrit, Greek, and Latin than any other living European language.

title: The Republic of Užupis
episode: Uzupis: The world's smallest republic in the middle of Vilnius | DW English
place: Constitution of the Republic of Užupis
description: On Užupis, a run-down neighborhood across the river that artists declared an independent republic on April 1, 1997, with its own president, anthem, and constitution, now on a wall in dozens of languages.

title: Daily life in the ghetto
episode: Daily Life in the Vilna Ghetto: Holocaust Survivor Testimonies
description: Survivors describe life in the two ghettos the Nazis created in Vilna’s old Jewish quarter in September 1941, where people kept schools, a library, and a theater going amid hunger and constant killings.

title: Fania’s Vilnius
description: A documentary following Fania Brantsovskaya, who escaped the Vilna ghetto in 1943 to fight with the Jewish partisans, and decades later worked as librarian of the Yiddish institute at Vilnius University.

title: Ponar
description: Scientists use radar to find a tunnel that prisoners dug with spoons to escape from Ponar, the forest outside Vilnius where about 70,000 Jews and thousands of others were shot from 1941 to 1944.

title: Independence, March 1990
episode: Western media news reports on Lithuania's 1990 declaration of independence
description: A compilation of American and British news reports from 1990, after Lithuania’s parliament declared independence on March 11, the first Soviet republic to do so, and Moscow answered with an economic blockade.

title: The night at the TV tower
episode: January 13th: A Somber Day In Lithuania
description: A Lithuanian explains January 13, 1991, when Soviet forces attacked the TV tower and crowds of unarmed people stood in their way. It is now the Day of the Defenders of Freedom, and the tower holds a small exhibition.
